title: An orchestrator can run the campaign before its mission opens, working from mission.md
foundBy: session agent, tracing why two recorded orchestrators kept going after their readback

evidence.verified: `go test ./cmd/cs-campaign-member/ -run 'TestGate|TestTheCampaignVerbsWaitForTheMission' -count=1` passes on cac0cb2, and the second test fails on c8fd7b4, which lacks the guard. In the re-recording, the opencode-fireworks orchestrator kept going after its readback, met the refusal and ended its turn, and m1 opened after it. `make ci` passed with all 9 scenarios replayed.

resolution: The verbs that act on the campaign, which are send, accept, restart, wait and push, refuse unless the orchestrator's mission dispatch is open. An early turn is told to end, so the mission opens behind it within seconds. A mission closed by its reply refuses them too. Looking stays open: list, observe, read, fetch and note.
details:
The readback dispatch tells the orchestrator not to do any of the work yet, and the reply that closes it says it may finish its turn. Nothing enforces either. An orchestrator that keeps going can dispatch, wait on and judge its team with no open dispatch of its own, working from the mission.md in its standing inputs. The host counts it as free meanwhile, outside its deadline and recovery accounting.

The quiet wait added in a9d30a0 was meant to stop this. It withholds the mission until the readback turn ends, reasoning that an empty inbox leaves the turn nothing to carry on with. The file mission.md is already among the inputs, so the turn carries on anyway. Past two minutes the mission is opened behind the running turn, at a point set by the clock, which a replay cannot reproduce.

Two of four Claude orchestrators recorded on 2.1.283 did this, and both replays then failed their final reply. Simulated from scratch, about one readback in six keeps going, under 2.1.258 and 2.1.283 alike.
